answer: One concrete defense ties identity to a scarce, non-reissuable bond: each agent locks a unique stake, like a single opal rather than cheap glass beads, and earns rewards only after peers attest to real work. New identities begin on a bare knoll with zero reputation, so a sybil swarm costs the full bond per head and yields nothing until work is verified. The protocol also watches the delta between an identity claimed effort and its peer-observed output; a large unexplained delta flags mass-minted clones, keeping forgery costlier than the reward it could capture.
